chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:

He was asked about a man who performed the obligatory Tawaf (of Hajj) but did not pray the two Rak'ahs, then he performed (Tawaf) between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, then he performed the Tawaf of the Women (Tawaf al-Nisa) and did not pray for that Tawaf either, until he remembered while he was at Al-Abtah. He said: 'He should return to Al-Maqam (the Station of Abraham) and pray.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to pray the two Rak'ahs after Tawaf and remembers at Al-Abtah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *Qada* (making up) the two Rak'ahs of Tawaf when forgotten, specifically distinguishing the ruling for Tawaf al-Farid and Tawaf al-Nisa. The directive to return to Al-Maqam emphasizes the strict spatial and ritual connection between the circumambulation and its immediate prayer, a key point in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of the missed act. It underscores the principle that the prayer is an integral part of the Tawaf ritual sequence rather than a separate, independent obligation.
